---
### Review — PR #6193 bacterial mannose PTS module audit

**Summary checklist**
- [x] Schema validation passes — *trusted, not re-run*: `just`/`uv` are unavailable in this sandbox, so I relied on the recorded proof in `analysis/module_audits/bacterial_mannose_pts/full-validation-proof.json`. All findings below are biology/curation judgment, not schema issues.
- [x] All PMIDs verified as real — every cited PMID resolves to a machine-fetched cache under `publications/` with matching title; the four newest (`9864311`, `40135874`, `38047704`, `12902269`) check out.
- [x] Supporting text matches publication content — spot-checked; e.g. the `12902269` growth quote is verbatim in `publications/PMID_12902269.md`, and `substrate-evidence.md:7` honestly records that the GlcNAc-6-P quote came from separately-acquired full text rather than the abstract-only cache.
- [x] GO terms correct and specific — labels verbatim; `GO:0022855/0022877/0022880` confirmed against the cached QuickGO records, and `GO:0051119`/`GO:0008982`/`GO:0016773` confirmed as ancestors of `GO:0022870` in `ua159-consultation/transporter-ancestry.json`. PANTHER labels match `interpro/panther/panther.obo` exactly.
- [ ] Review actions well-justified — three rows carry support that does not bear on the claim (below)
- [x] Core functions accurately identified — the IIA/IIB-vs-IIC/IID split is modelled correctly, with `contributes_to_molecular_function` used throughout for the complex-level activity
- [x] No over-annotation issues missed — the restraint is genuinely good: `GO:0005515` IPI removed per policy, lambda entry and bacteriocin receptor activity kept out, `GO:0022880` deliberately *not* extrapolated to IL1403

This is careful, well-provenanced work. The E. coli and *L. lactis* reviews are strong — targeted PMID quotes, honest distinction between native genetics and cross-species inference, and the `GO:1902495` NEW rows on manY/manZ are legitimately absent from GOA (verified against `manY-goa.tsv`/`manZ-goa.tsv`) and backed by PDB 6K1H. Three things should be fixed before merge.

---

### 🟡 IMPORTANT

**1. `PANTHER:PTHR32502` is asserted as the family `term` for two different roles, and the accompanying family review says it corresponds to neither**

`modules/bacterial_mannose_pts.yaml:411` (EIIC descriptor) and `:450` (EIID descriptor) both set `term: PANTHER:PTHR32502`. But `interpro/panther/PTHR32502/PTHR32502-review.yaml` establishes that this family is `HETEROGENEOUS`, that IIC and IID sit in *different* subfamilies (`SF4`/`SF25` for IIC, `SF5`/`SF27` for IID), and that the root is `TOO_DEEP` even for `GO:0009401` because it reaches into the soluble GatZ/KbaZ aldolase-support branch. One identifier cannot be what both descriptors mean.

The PR already applies the correct rule one role over: the EIIB descriptor (`:226`, `:358`) omits `term` entirely because "No single PANTHER family is established for all separate EIIB proteins". CLAUDE.md's instruction is the same here — *"If you cannot be sure, assert no id… an omitted id says 'not established'; a wrong id says something false, and says it in a machine-readable field other tooling will believe."* The prose caveat in `notes` is not machine-readable; the asserted `term` is.

Suggested fix: drop `term` from both membrane descriptors. `required_domain` (`InterPro:IPR004700` for IIC, `IPR004704` for IID) already does the discriminating work that PTHR32502 cannot, and `representative_members` keeps the proteins themselves. Do **not** substitute a subfamily id mechanically — no single subfamily covers both the E. coli and the lactococcal members. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20cmungall%2Faigr-mannose-pts-taxon-audit%2C%20in%20modules%2Fbacterial_mannose_pts.yaml%2C%20remove%20the%20%60term%3A%20PANTHER%3APTHR32502%60%20block%20from%20the%20%22mannose-active%20EIIC%20membrane%20partners%22%20family%20descriptor%20(around%20line%20411)%20and%20the%20%22mannose-active%20EIID%20membrane%20partners%22%20descriptor%20(around%20line%20450).%20Keep%20preferred_term%2C%20required_domain%20(InterPro%3AIPR004700%20and%20IPR004704%20respectively)%2C%20representative_members%20and%20notes.%20Rationale%3A%20interpro%2Fpanther%2FPTHR32502%2FPTHR32502-review.yaml%20establishes%20the%20family%20is%20HETEROGENEOUS%2C%20splits%20IIC%20and%20IID%20across%20different%20subfamilies%20(SF4%2FSF25%20vs%20SF5%2FSF27)%2C%20and%20is%20TOO_DEEP%20for%20GO%3A0009401%3B%20per%20CLAUDE.md%20an%20unestablished%20family%20term%20must%20be%20omitted%20rather%20than%20asserted.%20Do%20not%20substitute%20a%20subfamily%20id.%20Mirror%20the%20treatment%20already%20used%20for%20the%20EIIB%20descriptor.%20Then%20re-run%20just%20validate-modules.&repo=ai4curation/ai-gene-review)

**2. manL's plasma-membrane `ACCEPT` has no cited evidence that bears on localization**

`genes/STRMU/manL/manL-ai-review.yaml:44-63`. The three `supported_by` items are: `/note="PTS EIIB type-4"` (a domain feature, not a location), "Each protomer is composed of a ManY and ManZ" (about *E. coli* membrane components, not ManL), and `recommendations.md` with no quote. None asserts that ManL is at the plasma membrane. The underlying UniProt annotation is ARBA-only (`manL-uniprot.txt:39` — `Cell membrane {ECO:0000256|ARBA:ARBA00004236}`), which CLAUDE.md classifies as an unvetted prediction rather than support, and Q8DSC4 has no `FT TRANSMEM`. The `reason` concedes the point: *"inferred from cognate complex architecture and comparative ManX biochemistry, not direct UA159 imaging"*.

Contrast ptnAB (`ptnAB-ai-review.yaml:50-62`), where the identical `ACCEPT` is carried by native IL1403 mass-spec co-isolation from PMID:17284603 — that one is fine. For manL the analogous native evidence does not exist, so `KEEP_AS_NON_CORE` fits the stated reasoning, and `GO:0005886` should come out of `core_functions.locations` (`:307`) where the core activity has not been shown to happen. The same applies to the `GO:0016020` → `GO:0005886` MODIFY at `:138-159`, whose `supporting_entities` are the *soluble* EIIA-man signatures `IPR004701`/`IPR036662`.

**3. The three *S. mutans* reviews paste one anchored `supported_by` block onto every row, including a growth-phenotype quote under localization rows**

In `manL-ai-review.yaml`, anchors `*id002` / `*id003` / `*id001` are reused on the cytosol MODIFY (`:32-40`), the plasma-membrane ACCEPT, `GO:0009401`, `GO:0015761`, `GO:0016020` and `GO:0022870`. `*id002` is "grew more slowly than the wild-type strain in glucose but grew faster in mannose" — a growth-rate phenotype, which is not evidence for a subcellular compartment, and is in fact the *compensation* result the review elsewhere correctly warns against over-reading. Same pattern in `manM-ai-review.yaml:62-64` and `manN-ai-review.yaml:60-64`, where it leads the `GO:0009401` and `GO:0016020` rows.

The *L. lactis* reviews show the right shape: each row cites the quote that actually supports *that* claim (membrane rows get "IIC and IID together form a membrane-located complex…", process rows get the utilization phenotype). Please re-point the STRMU rows the same way rather than sharing one anchor set.

---

### 🔵 SUGGESTIONS

- **Quote the cached publications directly, not the audit's own excerpt file.** The STRMU rows cite `file:analysis/module_audits/.../source-excerpts.md` for text that is verbatim in `publications/PMID_12902269.md` (I confirmed both contain it). Citing the intermediary means the row no longer ties its quote to a paper, and PMID:12902269 is already in `references` with findings. The `file:` mechanism is right for the genuinely external full texts (as `substrate-evidence.md` does well) — just not for text we already have cached.
- **`enables` vs `contributes_to` on the membrane-only subunits.** manM/manN/ptnC/ptnD MODIFY `GO:0051119` to `enables`-qualified `GO:0022870`/`0022855`/`0022880` while the `reason` states "autonomous phosphotransfer by this membrane subunit is not asserted". `core_functions` correctly uses `contributes_to_molecular_function`; the row-level qualifier is the GO-sanctioned place to say the same thing (`ContributesToQualifierEnum` exists, and `source_defects` has a defect type for a wrong relation). Worth a sentence in `reason` noting the intended qualifier even if the row keeps GOA's.
- **`GO:0022880` rigor is asymmetric between the two panels.** manX's reason is scrupulous that `GO:0022880` *requires* the 6-phosphate product and cites PMID:9864311 Fig. 1 for it. The STRMU reviews propose the same term on uptake data alone. PMID:24928869 should be able to supply the S. mutans product-position evidence — cite it, or say explicitly that the product position is inferred.
- **PTHR32502 node taxon looks wrong upstream.** `PTHR32502-review.yaml:182-184` and `:206-208` record `node_taxon: NCBITaxon:1385 Bacillales` on `PTN002845864`/`PTN002845871`, whose seeds are the *E. coli* proteins P69801/P69805 (Enterobacterales). The review flags it in prose ("retained rather than used to override the actual mixed descendant tree"), which is the right call for the cached value — but it reads like a genuine PAINT defect worth reporting upstream rather than only noting locally.
- **Unused references.** `PMID:11976750` is in `PTHR33799-review.yaml:157` but never appears in a `supported_by` there (it is used in PTHR32502). `publications/PMID_41432198.md` (*Enterococcus lactis* Man-PTS) is added to the cache but cited nowhere — either use it for the taxon-scope argument or drop it.
- **manY's duplicate `GO:0009401` IDA row.** GOA carries two PMID:2951378 IDA rows differing only in qualifier (`involved_in` from ComplexPortal, `acts_upstream_of_or_within` from EcoCyc); the review has one, with no `qualifier` set (`manY-ai-review.yaml:384-397`). This predates the PR — `origin/main` has the same shape — so it is not a regression, but it does mean the "93 ordered source annotations preserved" claim is one short, and which of the two rows the surviving entry represents is ambiguous.

---

I've requested changes on items 1–3. Items 1 and 2 both come down to the same discipline the PR otherwise applies well — don't assert in a machine-readable field what the prose admits is unestablished.
 · branch [`cmungall/aigr-mannose-pts-taxon-audit`](https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/tree/cmungall/aigr-mannose-pts-taxon-audit)

### Review summary — bacterial mannose PTS module audit

Careful, well-provenanced work. The E. coli and *L. lactis* reviews are strong: targeted PMID quotes, honest separation of native genetics from cross-species inference, GO labels verbatim, ancestry checks cached, `GO:0005515` IPI removed per policy, and lambda entry / bacteriocin receptor activity correctly kept outside the transport module. The `GO:1902495` NEW rows on manY/manZ are genuinely absent from GOA and backed by PDB 6K1H.

Three items to fix before merge (details in the review comment):

**🟡 1. `PANTHER:PTHR32502` asserted as the family `term` for two different roles.** `modules/bacterial_mannose_pts.yaml:411` (EIIC) and `:450` (EIID) both carry it, while `interpro/panther/PTHR32502/PTHR32502-review.yaml` establishes the family is HETEROGENEOUS, splits IIC and IID across different subfamilies (SF4/SF25 vs SF5/SF27), and is TOO_DEEP even for GO:0009401. The PR already applies the correct rule to the EIIB descriptor by omitting `term`; do the same here. `required_domain` (IPR004700 / IPR004704) already does the discriminating work. Do not substitute a subfamily id mechanically.

**🟡 2. manL's plasma-membrane ACCEPT cites no evidence bearing on localization.** `genes/STRMU/manL/manL-ai-review.yaml:44-63` — the three supported_by items are a IIB domain FT note, an E. coli ManY/ManZ protomer quote, and an unquoted recommendations file. UniProt's location for Q8DSC4 is ARBA-only (`manL-uniprot.txt:39`) and there is no TRANSMEM. The reason itself concedes no direct UA159 evidence. `KEEP_AS_NON_CORE` fits, and GO:0005886 should come out of `core_functions.locations`. (ptnAB's identical ACCEPT is fine — it has native IL1403 mass-spec support.)

**🟡 3. The three S. mutans reviews share one anchored supported_by block across heterogeneous rows.** `*id002` ("grew more slowly than the wild-type strain in glucose but grew faster in mannose") leads the cytosol, plasma-membrane, GO:0009401 and GO:0016020 rows in manL/manM/manN. A growth phenotype is not evidence for a compartment. The L. lactis reviews show the right shape — re-point the STRMU rows per-claim.

🔵 Also suggested: quote the cached publications directly rather than the audit's own excerpt file where the text is already in `publications/`; note the intended `contributes_to` qualifier on the membrane-only subunits; supply S. mutans product-position evidence for GO:0022880 (manX is scrupulous about this, STRMU is not); report the PTHR32502 `node_taxon: Bacillales` on E. coli-seeded nodes as an upstream PAINT defect; drop or use the unused `PMID:11976750` / `PMID_41432198` references.

Note: `just`/`uv` are unavailable in this environment, so I did not re-run validation and relied on the recorded `full-validation-proof.json`. All findings above are curation judgment, not schema issues.
